prompt: Describe your typical workday. Speak for about 45–60 seconds. Include when you start, main tasks, and how you end the day.
rubric: Covers start, tasks, end of day
sampleAnswer: I usually start work around nine. In the morning I check emails and join a short standup with my team. Then I focus on project tasks until lunch. Afternoons are for meetings and finishing reports. I wrap up by updating our task board before leaving around six.
guidance: Use present simple for routines. Mention 3–4 concrete activities.

prompt: Talk about a business trip you have taken or would like to take. Where did you go (or want to go), and what was the purpose?
sampleAnswer: Last year I traveled to Singapore for a client workshop. We spent two days reviewing contract terms and touring their warehouse. The trip helped us build trust, and we closed a larger order the following month.
guidance: Include destination, purpose, and one outcome.

prompt: Recommend a restaurant to a visiting colleague. Mention the type of food, location, and why it is suitable for a business meal.
sampleAnswer: I'd recommend Harbor Bistro near the convention center. They serve modern Asian cuisine in a quiet setting, which is ideal for conversation. The lunch menu is reasonably priced, and service is usually fast.
guidance: Give 2–3 reasons; keep tone friendly and professional.

prompt: Explain how you prepare for an important meeting. List the steps you take before and during the meeting.
sampleAnswer: Before an important meeting, I review the agenda and prepare key talking points. I also check any data I might need. During the meeting I listen carefully, take notes, and confirm action items before we finish.
guidance: Use sequencing words: first, then, finally.

prompt: A coworker asks you how to write a polite follow-up email when a client has not replied. Give spoken advice with an example phrase.
sampleAnswer: I'd wait about three to five business days, then send a short follow-up. You can say, 'Just checking whether you had a chance to review the proposal I sent last week.' Keep it friendly and offer to answer questions.
guidance: Advise timing + tone + one sample sentence.

prompt: Describe a time you solved a problem at work. What was the problem, what did you do, and what was the result?
sampleAnswer: Once our printer failed right before a client presentation. I quickly switched to a backup printer on another floor and reformatted the slides for that paper size. We delivered on time, and the client never noticed the issue.
guidance: Use past tense: problem → action → result.

prompt: Give directions from a hotel to a nearby conference center. Include landmarks and approximate time on foot or by taxi.
sampleAnswer: From the hotel lobby, turn left onto Main Street and walk two blocks past the city library. The conference center is on your right, next to the blue fountain. It takes about ten minutes on foot, or three minutes by taxi.
guidance: Use turn left/right, go straight, next to, about X minutes.

prompt: You are ordering lunch for a team of six. Speak as if calling a restaurant: state the order, ask about delivery time, and give a delivery address.
sampleAnswer: Hello, I'd like to place a delivery order for six people: four club sandwiches and two vegetarian salads. Could you tell me how long delivery will take to 88 Market Street, 12th floor? We'd like it around 12:30 if possible.
guidance: Sound like a real phone order; include quantity and address.

prompt: Persuade your team to hold the next brainstorming session in person instead of online. Give two reasons.
sampleAnswer: I think we should meet in person for the next brainstorm. First, it's easier to sketch ideas on a whiteboard together. Second, people tend to stay more engaged when we're in the same room. We can still share notes online afterward.

prompt: Introduce yourself to a new international colleague on their first day. Include your name, role, and one tip about the workplace.
sampleAnswer: Hi, I'm Sara from the marketing team. Welcome to the office! If you need help with anything, feel free to ask. One tip: the best coffee machine is on the second floor near the windows.
guidance: Keep it warm and under 40 seconds.

prompt: Explain the difference between 'CC' and 'BCC' in email for a junior coworker who is new to business email.
sampleAnswer: CC means carbon copy—everyone can see who else received the email. BCC means blind carbon copy—recipients can't see those addresses. Use BCC when you email a large list and want to protect people's privacy.
guidance: Simple definition + when to use each.

prompt: A flight is delayed by two hours. Leave a voicemail for your client explaining the delay and proposing a new meeting time.
sampleAnswer: Hi Mr. Patel, this is Anna from BrightCo. My flight has been delayed by two hours, so I'll arrive later than planned. Could we move our meeting to 4 p.m. instead of 2? Please call me back when you can. Thanks.
guidance: Greeting → reason → new plan → callback request.

prompt: Summarize aloud the following data: Online sales rose 15% in Q3, store sales fell 4%, and customer satisfaction stayed at 92%.
sampleAnswer: In the third quarter, online sales increased by fifteen percent, while in-store sales decreased by four percent. Customer satisfaction remained steady at ninety-two percent.
guidance: Paraphrase; don't just read numbers robotically.

prompt: You have a food allergy. Explain to a server what you cannot eat and ask whether a dish can be prepared safely.
sampleAnswer: Hi, I have a peanut allergy. Could you tell me if the salad dressing contains nuts, and can the kitchen prepare my meal without any peanut products? I'd really appreciate it.
guidance: Be clear and polite; ask a yes/no safety question.

prompt: Give a 30–45 second opinion: Should companies allow employees to work from home three days a week? Support your view with one advantage and one possible drawback.
sampleAnswer: I support allowing three remote days a week. The main advantage is better focus and less commuting stress. One drawback is that teamwork can feel weaker if people rarely meet. Overall, a hybrid schedule works well when teams set clear core hours.
